cover.title: Why Is Renters Insurance So Cheap?
cover.label: renters policy

lines.text: Renters insurance costs about $14 a month. Insurers still profit.
lines.say: Renters insurance costs about fourteen dollars a month. Insurers still profit.

lines.text: The trick: it covers your stuff and liability, not the building.
lines.say: The trick is what's missing. It covers your stuff and your liability, not the building.

lines.text: Average renters premium: $173 a year (NAIC, 2023 data).
lines.say: State regulators put the average renters premium at a hundred seventy-three dollars a year in twenty twenty-three.
Divide that by twelve and you get fourteen dollars and forty-two cents a month.

lines.text: In 2014 it was $190, so the average actually went down.
lines.say: Back in twenty fourteen it was a hundred ninety dollars, so it actually went down.

lines.text: Allstate's other personal lines (with renters), 2025: 77.4¢ claims and 16.5¢ expenses per $1.
lines.say: Allstate reports renters alongside condo and landlord policies. In twenty twenty-five, each premium dollar there paid seventy-seven point four cents in claims and sixteen point five cents in expenses.
That leaves six point one cents of underwriting profit on every dollar.

lines.text: Two quiet extras: investing premiums before claims, and bundling with car insurance.
lines.say: Two quiet extras: insurers invest premiums before claims arrive, and renters policies help bundle in car insurance.

lines.text: Small risk, small price, steady profit. That's the renters model.

post.title: How Renters Insurance Makes Money on $14 a Month
post.ig:
Renters insurance costs about $14 a month. Insurers still profit.
The average renters premium was $173 a year in 2023, down from $190 in 2014 (NAIC).
It covers your stuff and liability, not the building, so the risk per policy is small.
Allstate's other personal lines, which include renters, paid 77.4 cents in claims and 16.5 cents in expenses per premium dollar in 2025: 6.1 cents of underwriting profit.
Sources: NAIC homeowners and renters reports; Allstate 10-K, fiscal 2025.
News and education, not financial advice.
